report_name: LOCAL CYCLING AND WALKING INFRASTRUCTURE PLAN TECHNICAL REPORT Penrith
how_pct_was_used: The PCT was used to validate identified desire lines, compare potential cycling demand scenarios, and inform the hierarchy of the suggested cycle network.
other_tools_developed: A prioritisation framework including 20 criteria across Effectiveness, Policy, Economic, and Deliverability categories, and the use of the DfT's Route Selection Tool (RST) and Early Assessment and Sifting Tool (EAST).
specific_evidence_of_impact: The LCWIP process has informed the prioritisation of infrastructure schemes, such as the Kemplay Bank Roundabout Improvements, and has been used to make the case for direct cycle and walking links (e.g., a flyover) through representations to National Highways during the development of the A66 Northern Trans-Pennine Project.
pct_usage_quote: The B5288, A592 and A6 converging on the town centre are the most popular routes in all current and future scenarios in the Propensity to Cycle Tool (PCT) (see www.pct.bike for further information on the PCT). These routes record more than 100 cyclists per day based on the ‘Go Dutch’ scenario, reflecting the potential growth for cycling within Penrith.
